question.text: Under the income-tax treatment applicable to PMS investors, are PMS fees and expenses deductible while computing capital gains?

answer.text: Yes, they are fully deductible against capital gains
No, PMS fees and expenses are not deductible while computing capital gains
They are allowed as tax credits against the final tax liability

explanation.text: The Logic: PMS fees and expenses are not deductible while computing capital gains. The investor recognises capital gains on the underlying transactions executed in the portfolio, but the management/performance fees and other portfolio-level expenses charged by the PMS provider cannot be claimed as a deduction from those capital gains. The Trap: Investors often assume that fees paid to the portfolio manager reduce the capital gain that is taxed. Under the position supported by the workbook, they do not. Note: Pages 159 and 164 of the NISM Series XXI-A PMS workbook support that PMS fees and expenses are not deductible while computing capital gains.
